title: Amplitude and Period
short: In y = A sin(Bx), the amplitude is |A| and the period is 2π/B.
trouble: Students take B as the period instead of 2π/B.

blocks.html: You know how to stretch and squeeze graphs: multiplying the output by $a$ stretches vertically, and replacing $x$ with $bx$ squeezes horizontally by a factor of $\frac{1}{b}$. Apply those moves to the sine wave and you control how tall the wave is and how long one cycle lasts.

For $\role{output}{y} = \role[amplitude]{coefficient}{A}\sin(\role[frequency factor]{frequency}{B}\role{input}{x})$ or $\role{output}{y} = \role[amplitude]{coefficient}{A}\cos(\role[frequency factor]{frequency}{B}\role{input}{x})$ with $B > 0$: the amplitude is $|A|$ and the period is $\dfrac{2\pi}{B}$.

Amplitude. Every height of $\sin(Bx)$ lies between $-1$ and $1$; multiplying by $A$ makes it lie between $-|A|$ and $|A|$. A negative $A$ also flips the wave upside down.
Period. One full cycle of sine needs its input to run from $0$ to $2\pi$. The input here is $Bx$, and $Bx$ goes from $0$ to $2\pi$ while $x$ goes from $0$ to $\frac{2\pi}{B}$. So a bigger $B$ packs cycles closer together and makes the period shorter.

opts.task: Make a wave with amplitude $2$ and period $\pi$.

blocks.cap: The dashed curve is $y = \sin x$. The green arrows mark one period; the red arrow is the amplitude.

blocks.title: Reading the numbers
blocks.q: Find the amplitude and period of $y = 3\sin(4x)$.
steps: So the wave rises to $3$ and repeats four times as often as $\sin x$.

blocks.title: A slow, flipped wave
blocks.q: Find the amplitude and period of $y = -2\cos\left(\frac{1}{2}x\right)$.
steps: Amplitude $= |-2| = 2$. The minus sign flips the wave: it starts at its lowest point, $-2$.
Period $= \dfrac{2\pi}{1/2} = 4\pi$, twice as long as usual.

blocks.title: Working backward
blocks.q: Write $y = A\sin(Bx)$ with $A, B > 0$, amplitude $5$ and period $6$.

blocks.html: Taking $B$ itself as the period, so that $y = \sin 4x$ would have period $4$. Bigger $B$ means more cycles in the same space, so the period must get smaller. Check: when $x$ equals one period, the input $Bx$ should equal exactly $2\pi$. For $\sin 4x$, $4 \cdot \frac{\pi}{2} = 2\pi$. ✓
